name: Escape / Prison Break
definition: Confined characters study a controlling system, prepare an exit, and cross successive thresholds while discovery and freedom acquire personal cost.
diagnostic_questions: Is overcoming confinement the central objective?
Does the controlling system have learnable rules and vulnerabilities?

neighbors.distinction: Escape applies operational ingenuity to getting out rather than taking a target.
Escape centers the agency of those confined; rescue centers an outside intervention.

reader_promises.name: Legible confinement
reader_promises.description: Make the barriers, routines, surveillance, and consequences concrete enough to strategize against.

reader_promises.name: Threshold tension
reader_promises.description: Turn each step toward freedom into a new exposure rather than one final door.

roles.name: Escape architect
roles.description: Maps the system and converts limited resources into a route.

roles.name: Essential companion
roles.description: Contributes a skill, need, or vulnerability that changes the escape design.

roles.name: Custodian
roles.description: Maintains confinement through routine, ideology, fear, or personal attention.

stakes: A life permanently shaped by captivity

movements.name: Confinement defined
movements.description: Establish rules, costs, and why ordinary compliance is no longer tolerable.

movements.name: Route built
movements.description: Acquire knowledge, trust, and resources while testing the system's responses.

movements.name: Breach
movements.description: Cross the first decisive barrier and trigger adaptation by the custodians.

movements.name: Free ground
movements.description: Resolve pursuit and define what freedom now requires or excludes.

complications.name: Route closed
complications.description: A learned vulnerability disappears because of policy, accident, or suspicion.

complications.name: Someone cannot leave
complications.description: A physical, emotional, or moral dependency makes the original plan insufficient.

complications.name: Early discovery
complications.description: Custodians detect preparation without understanding the complete route.

twists.name: Larger prison
twists.description: The first boundary conceals a broader system of control that was fairly signaled.

twists.name: Authorized exit
twists.description: The captor permits movement for a purpose that creates a subtler trap.

conclusions.name: Collective freedom
conclusions.description: The escape succeeds through cooperation and changes more than one captive's future.

conclusions.name: Solitary freedom
conclusions.description: One character escapes while separation or guilt defines the victory.

conclusions.name: Freedom redefined
conclusions.description: External escape fails or remains incomplete, but a decisive form of agency is recovered.

subversions: Make knowledge of people more useful than knowledge of architecture.
Let the escape expose how captives also maintained the system.
cliches_to_avoid: Guards becoming incompetent only during execution
A perfect route with no consequential tradeoff
quality_checks: The audience understands barriers before characters overcome them.
Preparation creates both capability and risk.
The ending defines freedom beyond physical distance.

sources.title: The Team Film Genre
sources.contribution: Analyzes group objectives, preparation, execution, crisis points, and escape-film examples.

sources.title: Movie Plot Analysis via Turning Point Identification
sources.contribution: Supports functional turning points based on changed plans, setbacks, and climax.
